title: A Study on Antibiotic Pattern of Urinary Tract Infections Causing Gram Negative Bacteria
author: Chittineni Krishna Prasad
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Collect midstream urine sample
steps.instruction: Obtain a midstream urine (MSU) specimen from each patient aged > 18 years who presents with symptoms of a urinary tract infection.

steps.title: Label and transport specimen
steps.instruction: Label the urine container clearly, place it in a self‑sealing polythene cover that has two compartments, put the laboratory requisition form in one compartment and the labeled sample in the other, and transport the package to the laboratory immediately.

steps.title: Inoculate agar plates
steps.instruction: Streak the urine sample onto three separate agar plates: Cysteine‑lactose electrolyte‑deficient (CLED) agar, MacConkey agar, and blood agar.

substeps.instruction: Prepare CLED agar plate and inoculate.
Prepare MacConkey agar plate and inoculate.
Prepare blood agar plate and inoculate.

steps.title: Incubate plates
steps.instruction: Incubate all inoculated agar plates at 37 °C for 48 hours.

steps.title: Identify bacterial growth
steps.instruction: Examine the incubated plates and identify any bacterial colonies according to the laboratory’s standard identification protocol.

steps.title: Perform Kirby‑Bauer susceptibility test
steps.instruction: Carry out antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby‑Bauer disc diffusion method on Mueller‑Hinton agar medium.
